key_insight: Training vision models with a human-like developmental ‘‘visual diet’’ causes them to rely more on shape than texture, producing substantially more robust visual inference without heavy computational cost.
problem_solved: Reduces texture bias and fragility to common corruptions in AI vision systems by shifting learned representations toward shape-based features using a resource-efficient training regimen.
method: Design a training ‘‘visual diet’’ inspired by human development (sampling and presentation patterns that mimic how infants see the world).
Train standard vision architectures on this developmental dataset and compare representations and performance to conventionally trained models.
Evaluate robustness and feature preference (shape vs. texture) across corruptions, adversarial-like perturbations, and transfer tasks.
impact: Provides a practical, data-centric route to more robust and generalizable vision models that can reduce reliance on massive compute or complex augmentations—appealing for practitioners seeking efficiency and reliability.

paper_title: Adopting a human developmental visual diet yields robust and shape-based AI vision
paper_authors: Zejin Lu, Sushrut Thorat, Radoslaw M. Cichy, Tim C. Kietzmann
